name: King of Assyria
overview: The King of Assyria mentioned in 2 Kings 23:29 is a male ruler known primarily as the adversary against whom Pharaoh Neco of Egypt fought. While the Bible does not specify his personal name, Clark's Commentary identifies him as Nabopolassar. This figure represents the Assyrian monarchy during a significant period of conflict involving Israel and Egypt.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Assyria' literally means 'king of Assyria,' reflecting his role as the sovereign leader of the Assyrian empire. This designation is a straightforward title rather than a personal name, indicating his political and military authority rather than a given name or divine naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for this person beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as the King of Assyria opposing Pharaoh Neco. There are no additional familial or relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: This King of Assyria is significant in the biblical narrative as a key figure opposing Egypt's Pharaoh Neco during a pivotal military engagement. His role underscores the geopolitical tensions impacting Israel and Judah at the time. Identifying him as Nabopolassar connects the biblical account to known historical figures, highlighting the interplay between biblical events and ancient Near Eastern history.
